angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 2,018,921 km at 23.82 pc = 1.13 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 81937: the Hipparcos parallax the radius was computed with (van Leeuwen 2007), 41.99 +/- 0.16 mas, inverted (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/746/1/101): 23.815 +/- 0.091 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 42.0904 +/- 0.1616 mas (same row, RUWE 3.62), 260.4 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 2.902 +/- 0.026 solar radii from Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 81937: radius in solar radii, from the limb-darkened angular diameter 1.133 +/- 0.009 mas (CHARA) and the Hipparcos parallax, 2.902 +/- 0.026 (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/746/1/101): 2,018,921 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.824 +/- 0.016 solar masses from Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 81937: mass in solar masses, from Yonsei-Yale isochrones at the measured radius and temperature (a model value), 1.824 +/- 0.016 (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/746/1/101); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 6693 +/- 45 K from Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 81937: effective temperature in K, from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux, 6693 +/- 45 (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/746/1/101). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 81937: effective temperature in K, from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux, 6693 +/- 45 (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/746/1/101)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/h-ursae-majoris.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 3.774, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's measured spectrum (Kharitonov, Tereshchenko & Knyazeva (1988), Spectrophotometric Catalogue of Stars (Alma-Ata), record 539) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
